deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page continues fol. 3r, 'Elegantiores Integralis ∫dx/√(1−x⁴) proprietates'. On that page Gauss defines s = sn(a) as the inverse of the lemniscatic integral, i.e. the lemniscatic sine sl(a). He defines c = cs(a) = sl(ϖ/2 − a), i.e. cl(a). He records the relation 1 = s²+c²+s²c², the addition theorems and the doubling formulas. Here 's.n' means sl(na) and 'c.n' means cl(na), both written as rational functions of s = sl a and/or c = cl a. In modern notation, with s' = √(1−s⁴) = c(1+s²), which follows from c² = (1−s²)/(1+s²):

(1) Multiples of the lemniscatic sine.
• sl a = s.
• sl 2a = 2sc(1+s²)/(1+s⁴) = 2sc(1+c²)/(1+c⁴). The second form holds because sl 2a = 2sc/(s²+c²) is symmetric in s and c.
• sl 3a = s(3 − 6s⁴ − s⁸)/(1 + 6s⁴ − 3s⁸).
• sl 4a = 4sc(1+s²)(1 − 5s⁴ − 5s⁸ + s¹²)/(1 + 20s⁴ − 26s⁸ + 20s¹² + s¹⁶).
  [My filling-in of the steps] Apply the doubling formula twice. With S = sl 2a one gets √(1−S⁴) = (1−6s⁴+s⁸)/(1+s⁴)². Then sl 4a = 2S√(1−S⁴)/(1+S⁴). The numerator is (1−6s⁴+s⁸)(1+s⁴) = 1−5s⁴−5s⁸+s¹². The denominator is (1+s⁴)⁴ + 16s⁴(1−s⁴)² = 1+20s⁴−26s⁸+20s¹²+s¹⁶.
• sl 5a = s·(5 − 2s⁴ + s⁸)/(1 − 2s⁴ + 5s⁸) · (1 − 12s⁴ − 26s⁸ + 52s¹² + s¹⁶)/(1 + 52s⁴ − 26s⁸ − 12s¹² + s¹⁶).
  This is the factorization of the degree-25 quintuplication polynomial s(5 − 62s⁴ − 105s⁸ + 300s¹² − 125s¹⁶ + 50s²⁰ + s²⁴) into a quadratic and a quartic in s⁴. The denominator is its 'reciprocal'. This factorization is exactly what underlies division of the lemniscate into 5 parts.

(2) General n (the novel item on the page). Gauss gives the beginning of a uniform expansion:
 sl(na) = s·[n − n(n²−1)(n²+6)/60·s⁴ − n(n²−1)(n⁶−13n⁴+36n²+420)/10080·s⁸ − …] / [1 + n²(n²−1)/12·s⁴ − n²(n²−1)(n²−4)(n²+75)/10080·s⁸ − …].
  The numerator and denominator coefficients of the multiplication polynomials are thus polynomials in n. I checked them against n = 1,…,5; for even n one must first expand √(1−s⁴). For example, the denominator s⁴-coefficients 1, 6, 20, 50 equal n²(n²−1)/12. The numerator s⁸-coefficients 0, −1/4, −1, −21/2, −105 agree with the formula.
  [My own check] I also verified the formula for all n against the Taylor series. Using arcsl s = s + s⁵/10 + s⁹/24 + … and sl u = u − u⁵/10 + u⁹/120 − …, sl(n·arcsl s) = ns − n(n⁴−1)/10·s⁵ + n(n⁴−1)(n⁴−5)/120·s⁹ + …. Gauss's ratio reproduces exactly these coefficients. The denominator coefficients are fixed by requiring N and D to be polynomials, i.e. by the pole structure.

(3) Multiples of the lemniscatic cosine.
• cl a = c.
• cl 2a = (1−2s²−s⁴)/(1+2s²−s⁴). This s-form is correct. The c-form should carry a minus sign: −(1−2c²−c⁴)/(1+2c²−c⁴).
• cl 3a = −c(3−6c⁴−c⁸)/(1+6c⁴−3c⁸). This follows from cl 3a = −sl(3b) with b = ϖ/2 − a and sl b = c.
  The scratch work at the bottom of the page derives it from cl(2a+a) = (cl2a·c − sl2a·s)/(1 + sl2a·cl2a·s·c). It uses s·sl2a = 2c(1−c²)/(1+c⁴), since s²(1+c²) = 1−c²; this is the displayed expression with the crossed-out 1+cc.
  The coefficient rows multiply lists out. Numerator: −(1−2c²−c⁴)(1+c⁴) = −1+2c²+0+2c⁶+c⁸, and −2(1−c²)(1+2c²−c⁴) = −2−2c²+6c⁴−2c⁶. These sum to −3+6c⁴+c⁸. Denominator: (1+2c²−c⁴)(1+c⁴) = 1+2c²+0+2c⁶−c⁸, plus −2c²+6c⁴−2c⁶−2c⁸. These sum to 1+6c⁴−3c⁸.
  He then rewrites the result in s, after a crossed-out attempt in c: cl 3a = c(1−4s²−6s⁴−4s⁶+s⁸)/(1+4s²−6s⁴+4s⁶+s⁸). [My check] Substituting c² = (1−s²)/(1+s²) turns the numerator into −4(1−4u−6u²−4u³+u⁴) and the denominator into 4(1+4u−6u²+4u³+u⁴), with u = s². The rows '−1−4+6−4−1' and '1+4−6+4+1' are these coefficient lists.
• cl 4a is written as a ratio of degree-8 polynomials in s² of the form N(u)/N(−u). The correct result is cl 4a = (1−8u−12u²−8u³+38u⁴+8u⁵−12u⁶+8u⁷+u⁸)/(1+8u−12u²+8u³+38u⁴−8u⁵−12u⁶−8u⁷+u⁸), with u = s². It is obtained from cl 4a = (1−2S²−S⁴)/(1+2S²−S⁴), S = sl 2a. Gauss's u³, u⁴, u⁵ coefficients have the wrong signs (see errors).

(4) Margin computations: these are logarithmic/antilogarithmic arithmetic for e^{π/2}.
• 7579868.62 is M·(π/1.8)·10⁷ with M = log₁₀e = 0.4342944819 (written 4342944.84). Its partial sums are 7504915.78 + 73303.82 + 1640.61 + 8.38 + 0.03.
• 0.9 × 7579868.62 = 6821881.76 = log₁₀ e^{π/2} = (π/2)M.
• Hence e^{π/2} = 4.8104773809, which appears repeatedly (4.8104779809, 48104773808, 481047380977, …).
• Bottom right: 6821882 + 1822648 = 8644530.
This is presumably preparation for q-series/theta values with q = e^{−π} for the lemniscatic case.
errors: c.2 written in c: Gauss gives (1−2cc−c⁴)/(1+2cc−c⁴), but cl 2a = −(1−2c²−c⁴)/(1+2c²−c⁴). At a = 0 (c = 1) his form gives −1 instead of 1. The same slip is on fol. 3r. The s-form (1−2ss−s⁴)/(1+2ss−s⁴) is correct. He evidently used the correct sign in the c.3 scratch computation, where he writes −(1−2−1).

c.4: the coefficients of s⁶, s⁸, s¹⁰ have the wrong sign in both numerator and denominator. Correct numerator: 1−8s²−12s⁴−8s⁶+38s⁸+8s¹⁰−12s¹²+8s¹⁴+s¹⁶. Correct denominator: 1+8s²−12s⁴+8s⁶+38s⁸−8s¹⁰−12s¹²−8s¹⁴+s¹⁶. As written, s² = 1/2 gives |cl 4a| ≈ 5.65 > 1, which is impossible; the correct value is −0.92154.
Margin: the second summand must be 73303.82, not 74303.82, and the '3' must be 0.03, for the sum 7579868.62 to come out. This may be a transcription issue rather than Gauss's error.
The two struck-out items, the cross before 20s¹² in s.4 and the first attempt at c.3 in terms of c, are self-corrected false starts. They are not errors in the final formulas.

results.what: Duplication formula sl 2a = 2 s c(1+s²)/(1+s⁴) = 2sc(1+c²)/(1+c⁴) and cl 2a in terms of s.
Triplication and quadruplication formulas for sl, and triplication for cl in both s- and c-form.
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (addition theorem, 1750s); systematized by Gauss (1797, unpublished) and Abel (1827)

results.what: sl 5a = s·(5−2s⁴+s⁸)(1−12s⁴−26s⁸+52s¹²+s¹⁶)/[(1−2s⁴+5s⁸)(1+52s⁴−26s⁸−12s¹²+s¹⁶)], i.e. the factorization of the quintuplication polynomial.
results.modern_name: Factorization of the lemniscatic 5-division polynomial (related to complex multiplication by 1±2i)
results.usually_credited_to: Abel (1827–28) in print; Gauss's lemniscate division (alluded to in Disquisitiones Arithmeticae §335, 1801)

results.what: General-n expansion: sl(na) = s[n − n(n²−1)(n²+6)/60 s⁴ − n(n²−1)(n⁶−13n⁴+36n²+420)/10080 s⁸ …]/[1 + n²(n²−1)/12 s⁴ − n²(n²−1)(n²−4)(n²+75)/10080 s⁸ …]. Numerator and denominator coefficients of the n-th multiplication polynomials are given as polynomials in n.
results.modern_name: Coefficients of the multiplication (division) polynomials of the lemniscatic/elliptic functions as polynomials in n; cf. later work on Abel/Eisenstein multiplication polynomials and elliptic division polynomials
results.usually_credited_to: General theory: Abel, Jacobi (Fundamenta Nova 1829), later Eisenstein; I know no standard attribution of these explicit coefficient polynomials

results.what: Logarithmic computation of e^{π/2} = 4.8104773809 via log₁₀ e^{π/2} = (π/2)·0.4342944819 = 0.6821881769.
results.modern_name: Numerical evaluation of e^{π/2} (Gelfond-type constant, relevant to lemniscatic q = e^{−π})
results.usually_credited_to: Routine computation; Gauss's lemniscatic numerics (1798–1800) are known from Werke III

deep.surprise_reason: This is Gauss's well-known early (c. 1797–98) lemniscatic material; the 'Elegantiores proprietates' text is printed in Werke III. The multiplication formulas and the factorized quintuplication formula match what is known of his lemniscate division work, which predates Abel. The only mildly notable item is the general-n interpolation of the multiplication-polynomial coefficients as polynomials in n, which checks against the Taylor series. It is a nice unpublished detail but not a major result, and it may already be in the Werke Nachlass.

checkable.asserts: s.3 satisfies the lemniscatic ODE for sl(3a): (d sl3a/da)² = 9(1−sl3a⁴), with ds/da = √(1−s⁴).
Gauss's general-n ratio agrees with sl(n·arcsl s)/s = n − n(n⁴−1)/10 s⁴ + n(n⁴−1)(n⁴−5)/120 s⁸ + O(s¹²).
Correct cl 4a in u = s². Gauss's version, with +8u³ −38u⁴ −8u⁵ in the numerator, fails this identity.
The two forms of cl 3a (in s and in c) agree, after dividing out the common factor c.
Evaluates to −1, so Gauss's c-form of cl 2a needs a minus sign, since cl 0 = 1.

transcription_corrections: s.4 denominator: the struck mark before 20s¹² is a cancelled sign; read '+20s¹²'.

s.nx numerator s⁸-term: read −(n⁶−13n⁴+36nn+420)·n·(nn−1)/10080, i.e. the factor after '420.' is n(n²−1), multiplying the whole bracket. The '[?]' can be removed; the reading is confirmed by the Taylor series check.

The first c.3 line is the result in c: '= −c(3−6c⁴−c⁸)/(1+6c⁴−3c⁸)'. In the second c.3 line, the struck attempt is in powers of c and the surviving form is in s: c(1−4ss−6s⁴−4s⁶+s⁸)/(1+4ss−6s⁴+4s⁶+s⁸).
Bottom expression: c(1−2cc−c⁴)/(1+2cc−c⁴) − (1−cc)·c·2/(1+c⁴). The crossed-out '1+cc' was the original denominator of (1−cc); this is the numerator of cl(2a+a).
c.4 denominator: the inked blots stand at the signs of 8s⁶ and 8s¹⁴. The transcription's reading '−8s⁶', '−8s¹⁴' is consistent with numerator(−u) form.
Margin: '74303.82' should probably read '73303.82', and '3' is the final 0.03, so that the column sums to 7579868.62.
